column12: Not a full labelled year of dosing: the same file shows 2,702 dosage units over those 267 beneficiaries, 10.12 syringes each, against the 13.04 a steady labelled year takes, which is what discontinuation_pct below measures. Scale for a reader: at the labelled 120 mg every 4 weeks a full year is 13 prefilled syringes. No Genentech WAC disclosure and no state transparency filing for Enspryng was found in this session, which is why the CMS basis is used rather than a list arithmetic

column11: a Part D anchor, so unlike the Part B products in this book the CMS figure is gross of manufacturer rebates and a real deduction applies. MedPAC, Report to the Congress June 2023, Chapter 2 'Assessing postsale rebates for prescription drugs in Medicare Part D': 'In 2021, manufacturer rebates averaged 23 percent of gross Part D spending, including spending for generics (which typically have no rebates)', and for drugs where the plan has no formulary alternative to threaten, 'sponsors were only able to negotiate rebates averaging less than 10 percent of gross prices'
column12: a judgement, and the weakest row in this file. Satralizumab had no approved competitor in its own disease when this spending was recorded, which is the protected-class case, so the figure is set at MedPAC's less-than-10-percent level rather than the 23% all-class average. The case for a larger deduction: the 23% average is diluted by generics that rebate nothing, so the brand-only average is higher, and Uplizna, Soliris and Ultomiris do compete in AQP4-positive NMOSD. Roche is not an SEC registrant and publishes no US gross-to-net reconciliation, so no company figure exists to replace this with

The Enspryng label (DailyMed setid 64c156a4-9bad-4d45-a294-0733c141f47b) gives 120 mg subcutaneously at weeks 0, 2 and 4 then 120 mg every 4 weeks, so a steady labelled year is 365/28 = 13.04 syringes. 10.12/13.04 = 0.7763 of a labelled year, and 1 - 0.7763 = 0.2237
column12: Judgement on method, and it leans low. column11: two shares multiplied. (1) Age: SHIELD DMD (NCT06450639) enrols males aged 8 to under 18. MD STARnet's four-state prevalence survey on 1 January 2007 ('Prevalence of Duchenne/Becker Muscular Dystrophy Among Males Aged 5-24 Years - Four States, 2007', MMWR 2009;58(40):1119-1123, Table 1) counted 349 cases aged 5 to 24, of which 220 were aged 10 to 19: 63.04%, taken as the proxy for the trial's 8-to-under-18 window. (2) Corticosteroids: the trial requires daily oral corticosteroids, and of 373 males with Duchenne followed by MD STARnet over 2000-2015, 'Overall, 75.6% were offered and 68.9% used corticosteroids' (Thomas S, 'Trends in Corticosteroid Use Among Males With Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy (DMD) During 2000-2015: Data From the MD STARnet', MDA Clinical and Scientific Conference abstract library). 0.6304 x 0.689 = 0.4343
column12: the shakiest layer row in this file and it leans high in two places. The MMWR age distribution counts Duchenne and Becker dystrophy together, and Becker's milder course puts more of its patients in the older bands, so the 10-to-19 share of Duchenne alone is probably higher than 63% - that biases low. Against it: the denominator is ages 5 to 24, while the book's 6,000 is every age, so boys under 5 and men over 24 are outside the MMWR count and dividing by the all-age pool overstates the share. And 68.9% 'used' corticosteroids at some point, where the trial needs daily use at enrolment. What would settle it: an MD STARnet age-specific prevalence table for Duchenne alone and a point-prevalence corticosteroid figure

column11: a judgement for an anti-IL-6 receptor antibody added on top of corticosteroids in a disease where the approved products target the dystrophin defect itself (exon-skipping antisense oligonucleotides and delandistrogene moxeparvovec) rather than the steroid-driven bone fragility SHIELD DMD measures, so it would not be displacing them. Set against that, SHIELD DMD is a 30-participant open-label single-arm study whose primary outcome is a change in bone and muscle measures rather than a clinical endpoint, which is a thin basis for a paediatric chronic antibody to reach a large share of a 6,000-patient disease

column11: the relapsing share. METEOROID (NCT05271409) enrols patients with at least one relapse in the preceding 12 months or at least two attacks in the preceding 24 months, and relapse prevention is what the drug is being filed for, so a monophasic patient is not in the treated population. Human M, Gilmartin CGS, Papathanasiou A, et al., 'Clinical Prognostic Factors Associated With Relapsing Myelin Oligodendrocyte Glycoprotein Antibody-Associated Disease: A Multicenter Cohort Study', Neurol Neuroimmunol Neuroinflamm 2026;13(6):e200651, doi:10.1212/NXI.0000000000200651, PMID 42673556: of 101 patients across three centres, 43 (42.6%) had a relapsing course and 58 (57.4%) were monophasic
column12: the published range for this share is wide and it moves with how long a cohort is watched: the same paper reports 54.5%, 48.7% and 37.9% at its three sites, and other series report 47% at 6 to 24 months of follow-up against 72% beyond five years. 42.6% is the pooled figure of the cohort with the longest relapsing-arm follow-up (median 77 months) and sits in the lower half of that range. A second narrowing is not priced and biases this high: METEOROID enrols from age 12, and about 30% of MOGAD is paediatric, so some of the under-12 population is outside the label this would be granted on

column11: a judgement. The case for a high share: there is no approved treatment for MOGAD at all, METEOROID is the first positive Phase 3 in the disease, the effect is large (87% relapse-free at 48 weeks against 67% on placebo, relapse risk down 68%, p=0.0025; Genentech press release 15108, 2026-04-21), and the product is a self-administered subcutaneous injection every four weeks. The case for a low one, which is why the number is not higher: the incumbents are cheap off-label generics (rituximab, mycophenolate, azathioprine, IVIG), and Enspryng's own penetration of its approved disease is thin - 267 Medicare Part D beneficiaries in 2024 (CMS Spending by Drug) against a US AQP4-positive NMOSD population in the thousands
